def: The quality or state of being soft; -- opposed to Ant:hardness, and used in the various specific senses of the adjective.
In a rural manner; as in the country.

To enter; to penetrate; to make a way into or throughsomething, as a pointed instrument does; -- used literally andfiguratively.And pierced to the skin, but bit no more. Spenser.She would not pierce further into his meaning. Sir P. Sidney.

Unfavorable; not commendatory; -- opposed to eulogistic.There is no course of conduct for which dyslogistic or eulogisticepithets may be found. J. F. Stephen.The paternity of dyslogistic -- no bantling, but now almost acentenarian -- is adjudged to that genius of common sense, JeremyBentham. Fitzed. Hall.
Making or producing myths; giving rise to mythical narratives.The mythopoeic fertility of the Greeks. Grote.
A genus of fossil trees of the Devonian and Carboniferous ages,having the exterior marked with scars, mostly in quincunx order,produced by the separation of the leafstalks.
